source_snapshot.title: fix(php): resolve imports by namespace, with clause-scoping and DoS fixes
source_snapshot.body:
Carries **@Hiro-Chiba's #442** plus three review fixes, one a DoS. Landing it here closes #442 as merged.

> ⚠️ **Merge with a merge commit, not squash** — contains Hiro-Chiba's two commits alongside mine.

## Their change (`ea79b11`, `83079ff`)

Resolves explicit PHP type imports by declared namespace instead of a repo-wide short-name match. The follow-up replaces the flagged ReDoS regex with a char-code trim — **the CodeQL alert on #442 is stale** and can be dismissed after a re-scan.

## My fixes

**1. `5c322a9` — the capture also matched the alias.** Confirmed against the grammar by dumping the parse tree: in `namespace_use_clause` the alias is a **direct `(name)` sibling** of the `qualified_name`, so `[(qualified_name) (name)]` captured both. `use Vendor\Package\User as Admin;` emitted an `IMPORTS` edge to an unrelated `Admin` class and promoted the wrong short-name matches from 0.5 to **0.9** — the opposite of this PR's purpose. Anchored to the clause's first named child; bare `use GlobalThing;` is a lone `(name)` child and still matches.

Two related bugs shared that root cause: `importAliased` was computed from the whole statement, so one alias in a comma-separated `use` disabled FQCN resolution for every clause; and that same unanchored `/\s+as\s+/` was a second ReDoS instance CodeQL missed (~3.7 s on a `use` padded with 100k spaces, which is valid PHP). Reading the clause node removes both.

**2. `663c6ce` — two regressions measured against main, not inferred.**
- A `use` leaked across braced namespace blocks: `go()` in `namespace B` resolved to the vendor file at 0.9 although `B` declares its own `Thing` two lines up. main emits no edge at all.
- Duplicate `CALLS` edges reached the graph: `phpCallKind` splits the dedup key, so `log()` and `Logger::log()` survive as two relationships; when both resolve to the same member, patch-builder salted the edge id by call kind and emitted two `UpsertEdge` ops with identical src/dst/predicate but different ids — and the dedup downstream keys on id. Measured main 1 op, this branch 2.

**3. `7c8a387` — one ordinary PHP file hung ingestion (the DoS).** `phpNamespaceForNode` rescanned the file's top-level nodes for every definition. A valid PSR-12 file — `namespace App\Support` plus ~16k functions, 890 KB, under the 1 MB cap — took **over three minutes**. `.php` is ingested by default, the minified-file skip needs a ≥20k-char line, and `ParsePool` has no per-file timeout, so one file pins a worker; PHP is also in `PARSER_DERIVED_PRESCAN`, so it's parsed twice.

| declarations | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| 2,000 | 3,245 ms | 104 ms |
| 4,000 | 13,099 ms | 151 ms |
| 8,000 | 54,408 ms | 236 ms |

Entity counts and `packageScope` values identical at every size.

Worth flagging, since it wasn't what I first assumed: mutation testing showed the binary search is *not* load-bearing, and even rebuilding the span list per definition stays fast. The dominant cost is `namedChild(i)` materializing a node wrapper per index — iterating `namedChildren` once is the real fix. The regression test times out only against the exact original.

## Known gap, not fixed here

My multi-namespace guard counts distinct `packageScope` strings, so it misses two blocks sharing a name and a `use`-only block. Cheap follow-up: count the `module` entities the parse already emits per braced block.

## Verification

Every fix mutation-tested. core-ingestion 338 passed, 6 pre-existing failures unchanged from base; `tsc --noEmit` clean.

changed_files.patch:
@@ -1026,9 +1026,13 @@ export const PHP_QUERIES = `
 
 ; ── Imports: use statements ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
 ; Simple: use App[local-path]\User;
+; The leading anchor pins the capture to the clause's FIRST named child. In
+; "use A[local-path]\C as Alias" the alias is a sibling (name) of the (qualified_name),
+; so an unanchored alternation would capture it too and emit a phantom import
+; of Alias. "use GlobalThing;" is a lone (name) child and still matches.
 (namespace_use_declaration
   (namespace_use_clause
-    (qualified_name) @import.source)) @import
+    . [(qualified_name) (name)] @import.source)) @import
 
 ; ── Function/method calls ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 ; Regular function call: foo()

commits.message:
fix(php): scope use-clause parsing to the clause, not the statement

Two defects, one root cause: both the query and the alias flag looked at the
whole 'use' declaration instead of the individual clause.

1. Phantom imports. In 'use Vendor[local-path]\User as Admin' the alias is a
   direct (name) sibling of the (qualified_name), so the unanchored
   alternation captured it as a second imported module. Ix then matched
   'Admin' against an unrelated class of that name, emitting an IMPORTS edge
   the file never declares and promoting the wrong short-name matches from
   0.5 to 0.9 — the exact class of error this PR exists to remove. Anchoring
   the capture to the clause's first named child fixes it; a bare
   'use GlobalThing;' is a lone (name) child and still matches.

2. Comma-separated imports. importAliased came from a regex over the whole
   statement, so 'use A[local-path]\Alpha, A[local-path]\Beta as Bee;' flagged every clause
   as aliased and silently disabled FQCN resolution for Alpha. Reading the
   clause node instead scopes it correctly.

Deriving the flag from the node also deletes an unanchored /[local-path]\s+/ over
repo-controlled text — the same polynomial-backtracking class CodeQL flagged
at phpTypeFqcn, in a spot it did not flag. Measured at ~3.7s on a use
statement padded with 100k spaces, which parses as valid PHP.

The two anchored kind regexes (^use function, ^use const) are linear and
unchanged.

core-ingestion: 334 passed, 6 pre-existing failures unchanged from base.

fix(php): scope use to its namespace block, and stop double-emitting calls

Two further regressions against main, both measured rather than inferred.

1. A use leaked across braced namespace blocks. phpFqcnImportsByLocal is
   keyed by file, but a use is scoped to its namespace block. Given

     namespace A { use Vendor[local-path]\Thing; function run(Thing $t) {...} }
     namespace B { class Thing {} function go(Thing $t) {...} }

   go() resolved to Vendor/Package/Thing.php at 0.9, though B declares its
   own Thing right there. main emits no edge for go at all. One namespace per
   file is the PSR-12 norm, so the index now skips a multi-block file rather
   than mis-resolve it, restoring main's behaviour exactly for that shape.

2. Duplicate CALLS edges reached the graph. phpCallKind splits the per-file
   dedup key, so log() and Logger::log() survive as two relationships. When
   both resolve to the same member, patch-builder salted the edge id by call
   kind and emitted two UpsertEdge ops with identical src, dst and predicate
   but different ids — and the dedup downstream keys on id, so both commit.
   Measured: main 1 op, this branch 2. The salt still applies when the two
   kinds resolve to different nodes, which is what it is for.

Both mutation-tested: each guard removed reds exactly its own test.
core-ingestion: 336 passed, 6 pre-existing failures unchanged from base.

fix(php): resolve a definition's namespace without rescanning the file

phpNamespaceForNode walked rootNode.namedChild(0..i) for every definition, so
one file cost O(definitions x top-level nodes). An ordinary, valid PSR-12 file
— namespace App\Support plus ~16k functions, 890 KB, comfortably under the
1 MB ingest cap — took over three minutes to parse, and nothing stops it:
.php is ingested by default, the minified-file skip needs a >=20k-char line,
and ParsePool has no per-file timeout, so one file pins a worker. PHP is also
in PARSER_DERIVED_PRESCAN, so the file is parsed twice.

Collect the unbraced namespace boundaries once per parse, mirroring how
goPackage is already hoisted, and binary-search them per definition. Braced
namespaces scope by containment and keep using the ancestor walk.

Measured on this machine, same file, entity counts and packageScope values
identical at every size:

  declarations   before      after
     2,000       3,245 ms    104 ms
     4,000      13,099 ms    151 ms
     8,000      54,408 ms    236 ms

Worth recording what mutation testing showed, since it is not what I first
assumed: swapping the binary search back for a linear scan over the spans
changes nothing, and even rebuilding the span list per definition stays fast.
The dominant cost is namedChild(i), which materializes a node wrapper per
index; iterating namedChildren once is what actually fixes it. The regression
test times out only against the exact original.

core-ingestion: 338 passed, 6 pre-existing failures unchanged from base.

chore: use the \\x00 escape instead of a raw NUL byte

I used raw NUL separators in a lookup key. They are invisible in most editors
and diffs — they render as a space — so the CI guard is the only thing that
sees them, and it is there precisely because a raw NUL makes the file binary
to grep/ripgrep, which then silently skips it.

The escape is the same byte at runtime, so behaviour and tests are unchanged.

fix(php): don't emit duplicate claims for a two-kind call

Same root cause as the duplicate edge fixed earlier in this branch, on the
claim path this time, and it fires on ordinary untyped PHP rather than an
exotic shape: phpCallKind splits the relationship dedup key, so
`handle(); $obj->handle();` survives as two relationships. A claim carries no
kind, so the two ops are byte-identical and nothing downstream can tell them
apart. Applied to both buildPatch and buildPatchWithResolution.

Contained today — stripMapModeOps drops all claims, so `ix map` never carried
these, and the only other consumer is a counter — but it inflates the counter
and would double-assert on any path that keeps claims.

Also tightens the namespace-scoping perf test from a 10s to a 3s timeout: the
fixed code runs in ~3ms and the old algorithm took ~12s, so 10s left only a
1.2x margin over the thing it is meant to catch.

Mutation-tested. core-ingestion: 339 passed, 6 pre-existing failures unchanged.

fix(php): count namespace blocks at the parser, not from entity scopes

The multi-namespace guard skipped a file when its entities carried more
than one distinct packageScope. Two shapes slip past that:

  namespace A { use Vendor\Thing; }   // declares nothing -> no scope
  namespace B { class Thing {} ... }

  namespace A { use Vendor\Thing; }   // two blocks, one scope *string*
  namespace A { class Thing {} ... }

In both, `use` from the first block was applied to the second, resolving
a name the second block declares itself and pointing it confidently at
the wrong file — the exact mis-resolution the guard exists to prevent.

Count `namespace_definition` nodes instead, which is what the guard
actually means. The count rides along on the walk that already collects
the unbraced spans: reading `namedChildren` a second time would pay the
node-wrapper materialization cost twice, and that term is what made the
original per-definition scan expensive.

`phpNamespaceBlocks` is spread in rather than assigned `undefined` so the
key is absent on non-PHP results — a present-but-undefined key still
serializes and would have rewritten every checked-in parseFile snapshot.

comments.body:
Added one more commit (`83b9be4`) after re-auditing the multi-namespace guard I wrote earlier in this PR. The guard was wrong in two reproducible ways.

It skipped a file when its entities carried more than one distinct `packageScope`. Two shapes slip past that:

```php
namespace A { use Vendor\Thing; }   // declares nothing -> contributes no scope
namespace B { class Thing {} ... }

namespace A { use Vendor\Thing; }   // two blocks, one scope *string*
namespace A { class Thing {} ... }
```

In both, the `use` from the first block was applied to the second — resolving a name the second block declares itself and pointing it confidently at the wrong file, which is precisely what the guard exists to prevent. Confirmed against real parser output before changing anything; the entity side genuinely cannot distinguish these.

It now counts `namespace_definition` nodes at the parser, which is what the guard actually means. The count rides along on the walk that already collects the unbraced spans — reading `namedChildren` a second time would pay the node-wrapper materialization cost twice, and that term is what made the original per-definition scan expensive.

Two tests cover the shapes above and a third asserts the common single-namespace file is still indexed, so "skip the ambiguous file" cannot quietly become "skip every file". All three go red against the old guard; the other 80 in the file stay green.

One near-miss worth recording: `phpNamespaceBlocks` is spread in rather than assigned `undefined`, because a present-but-undefined key still serializes and would have rewritten every checked-in `parseFile` snapshot — including TypeScript ones. That was invisible locally, since `doctor.ts`'s snapshot already fails on `main` for an unrelated reason and the failure *count* was unchanged. Verified the received parse result for `doctor.ts` is now byte-identical to `main`.

I reviewed the changes in #446 and independently reproduced the two multi-namespace cases the guard needs to handle:

- **Two braced blocks sharing one namespace name.** The entity-side guard added in `663c6ce` saw one distinct `packageScope` string (`size === 1`) and let the file through — applying one block's `use` to the other.
- **A `use`-only braced block.** It declares no type definitions, so it contributes no `packageScope` entry at all, yet its imports are still confined to it.

I validated a fork implementation against these cases: `0701040` (branch `fix/446-multi-namespace-guard`) counts namespace-definition module entities — excluding import-use modules via their IMPORTS relationships — instead of distinct scope strings, with two regression tests. The `resolveEdges` suite passes **82/82** against it.

The entity-count approach works, but it reconstructs the count from generated entities: it assumes every braced block (including use-only ones) emits a `kind:'module'` entity and that import-use modules stay identifiable. `83b9be4` removes that coupling — `phpNamespaceBlocks` counts the tree-sitter `namespace_definition` nodes directly, on the same single walk that already collects the unbraced spans (from `7c8a387`), so it cannot drift if entity emission changes and costs nothing extra. The same suite passes **83/83** against `83b9be4`.

For context, the guard's evolution is worth noting: `663c6ce` introduced the entity-side version; `7c8a387` replaced per-definition top-level scans with one precomputed walk + binary search (~197s → ~355ms on a ~16k-function PSR-12 file); `b07bff36` replaced a raw NUL byte with the `\x00` escape; `e786f20` deduplicates byte-identical claims for two-kind calls; `83b9be4` lands the parser-level count as the final form.

The fork branch is offered only as independent validation of the two shapes — not as a competing fix.

Quick clarification on the earlier fork references: the historical commits [`13b7bf0`](https://github.com/Alot1z/Ix-remap/commit/13b7bf0cc24cce7680ca5869be9f395894b03ff8), [`82aeb28`](https://github.com/Alot1z/Ix-remap/commit/82aeb285c3bc3ab516d0a7d1899ffee95bb52a40), and [`ece8195`](https://github.com/Alot1z/Ix-remap/commit/ece8195d71c439a69e79098ec8e3befe915532b7) were fork-side audit/communication artifacts and are not part of the #446 implementation. The current #446 implementation and regression coverage are contained in the upstream PR itself; the separate [`6a50e6c`](https://github.com/Alot1z/Ix-remap/commit/6a50e6cb2ab0790f0c594962f89e59ca6464dd70) fork commit is only an independent validation artifact. No changes to the #446 implementation are required from that validation.

Found one remaining PHP namespace-scope regression while adversarially re-auditing #446: `phpNamespaceBlocks` counts namespace-definition blocks but does not represent the global↔namespace boundary, so mixed-scope files could let the per-file FQCN import map cross that boundary and emit an incorrect high-confidence `CALLS` edge.

`0a7d97f` adds the minimal parser-level guard and regression coverage for the affected braced, unbraced, decoy, and reverse-direction cases. The relevant resolveEdges/query/patch-builder tests pass 113/113, with the regression reproduced against `83b9be4` before the fix and eliminated afterward.

Commit: https://github.com/Alot1z/Ix-remap/commit/0a7d97f6213e567bcd074ebe7fb41cd32b77e7c3

Found and independently verified one more PHP resolution regression in the current #446 implementation: `phpTypeFqcn` drops any entity carrying a `container`, and `findEnclosing`'s inclusive line ranges falsely nest two same-line sibling declarations — so `<?php namespace Vendor\Package; class A {} class B {}` plus `use Vendor\Package\B; new B()` resolves to nothing (NONE) both in-batch and through the global index, where base `043bc68` emitted IMPORTS @0.9.

The issue is still reproducible against the current upstream PR state (head `83b9be4`), and I did not find an existing fix or duplicate PR addressing it.

Follow-up commit `f577492` applies the minimal fix — drop the `entity.container` exclusion in `phpTypeFqcn`/`ambiguousPhpTypeNames`; PHP types (class/interface/trait/enum) can never be members, so a container on one is always a same-line artifact — and adds regression coverage for the same-line positive and multi-line control, in-batch and cross-batch.

Verification: resolveEdges/queries.php/patchBuilder.resolution 115/115, `tsc` clean; the regression reproduces against `83b9be4` and is eliminated after.

Follow-up commit (on top of `0a7d97f`, surfaced in the earlier comment):
https://github.com/Alot1z/Ix-remap/commit/f577492219d9b0546df8996d6679784e3c465b99

This is ready for the PR author/maintainer to review/cherry-pick.
